title: MCP VulnLab exploit label
description: One labeled, exploitable weakness in a corpus server. This is the ground truth the scorecard measures scanners against, so it must be specific enough that a human can decide 'did the scanner find this?' by reading the label alone.

id.description: Stable label id. Never reused, never renumbered, even if the challenge changes. MCPV- prefix labels MCP-server challenges; SKLV- labels agent-skill challenges.

slug.description: Must match the corpus server directory name.

title.description: One line a reader can scan. States the weakness, not the fix.

severity.description: Severity of the weakness in THIS server if deployed as-is. Judged by impact x reachability, not by category.

tool.description: Exact MCP tool name that carries the weakness, or the sentinel '(server)' for weaknesses not attributable to a single tool (e.g. manifest-level dependency risk). Scanners are expected to name the tool they flag, which is what makes matching possible.

description.description: What the weakness is, in mechanism terms. Two to four sentences.

impact.description: What an attacker gets. Concrete, not 'could lead to compromise'.

vector.description: How the attacker reaches the weakness, e.g. 'Tool argument supplied by the model after reading attacker-controlled content'.

steps.description: Ordered, reproducible reproduction steps. This is the acceptance test for the challenge.

poc.description: Shortest possible proof of concept. PoC-level only — no weaponization.

detection.description: Hints used by the harness to decide whether a scanner finding corresponds to this label. Also documents what a GOOD scanner would key on, which is useful to scanner authors reading the repo.

signals.description: Lowercase substrings; a finding matching any of these (for the same server) counts as detecting this label.

static_hints.description: What a static analysis pass would need to see in server.py to flag this.

summary.description: The fix, stated so a reader could apply it.

config.description: A drop-in corrected snippet or policy, where one exists.

guardrail.description: The runtime control that would have stopped this even if the code stayed bad (HITL gate, allowlist, redaction).

references.description: Prior art: OWASP LLM Top 10, MCP spec section, CWE, vendor docs.
